Items.Authors: Félix Gudin, Nicolas Forget
Items.Title: Broadband heterodyne detection with ultrafast laser for stellar interferometry
Items.Abstract: Heterodyne interferometry enables coherent signal combination from distant telescopes, but its use at optical wavelengths is limited by photodetector electronic bandwidth. Using a mode-locked femtosecond laser to generate a train of highly chirped pulses as the Local Oscillator (LO), instead of a single-frequency laser, allows wideband detection over ~1 THz of optical bandwidth with a single detection channel. The method scales easily to multichannel detection with the same LO. We demonstrate this using a two-arm, fiber-based heterodyne interferometer in the H-band (1.56 µm) with a single detection channel. The system uses telecom-grade components, 22 GHz photodetectors, and a digital oscilloscope. Fringe visibility is retrieved through direct numerical correlation without electronic delay lines. The achieved SNR allows observing the brightest H-band stars with ~1 m² collecting area telescopes and short integration time (<100 ms).

Items.Authors: Pietro Ferraiuolo, Runa Antonio Briguglio Pellegrino, Guido Agapito, Jean-Pierre Véran
Items.Title: Building a catalog of close binary stars through GAIA PSF simulations for ELT era AO systems
Items.Abstract: Close binary stars with separations of 20–200 mas can distort NGS asterisms, introduce centroiding bias, and reduce the stability and performance of adaptive optics systems. The BINCAT project aims to build a dedicated catalog of such binaries to support AO operations, serving both as a blacklist for NGS selection and as a benchmark set for testing next-generation systems. Because resolving binaries at these separations requires ≥8 m telescopes with AO, we identify candidates by exploiting Gaia DR3 binarity indicators and by developing a simulator capable of reproducing Gaia’s detection flags. The simulator provides the probability of binarity and estimates key parameters such as separation and magnitude contrast. Candidate binaries can then be validated through commissioning data from instruments at the ELT (MORFEO/MICADO, ANDES), other AO-equipped facilities, and archival observations, enabling iterative refinement of the catalog.

Items.Authors: Scott MacDonald, Jenny Atwood
Items.Title: Calcium fluoride lens acceptance testing for the Gemini Infrared Multi-Object Spectrograph
Items.Abstract: Calcium Fluoride optics continue to serve an important role in infrared astronomical instrumentation due to their broad transmission and cryogenic performance. Acceptance testing on an uncoated Calcium Fluoride lens using a Zygo 4" Qualifire 2.4 interferometer. The work focused on verifying surface figure, radius of curvature, and optical quality.

Items.Authors: Davide Mollica, Osvaldo Catalano, Giovanni Contino, Milvia Capalbi, Mattia Corpora, Fabio P. Lo Gerfo, Pierluca Sangiorgi, Giuseppe Sottile, Francesco Casini, Stefano Germani, Giuseppe Leto, Teresa Mineo, Gino Tosti, Salvatore Scuderi, Giovanni Pareschi
Items.Title: Calibration of the ASTRI-1 and ASTRI-3 Cherenkov cameras
Items.Abstract: The ASTRI Mini-Array is an international project, led by the Italian National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF), that aims to deploy an array of nine 4 m-diameter Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes. It is designed to study astronomical sources emitting in the very high-energy range, from 1 TeV to 200 TeV. We have installed seven telescopes out of nine, and two of them already acquire Cherenkov data, undergoing the commissioning and science verification phase. Each telescope is equipped with a Cherenkov camera based on Silicon Photomultipliers, which features an embedded calibration system that consists of two laser diodes coupled to a side-emitting optical fiber. This system enables on-site extraction of calibration coefficients for data analysis and camera configuration. In this contribution, we describe the camera calibration performed during the commissioning phase of the two operational telescopes and the system stability monitoring conducted through daily calibration run

Items.Authors: Breann N. Sitarski, Jessie L. Dotson, Jonathan C. Papa, Paul A. Scowen, Scott Gaudi, Milan Mandić, Alan B. Gostin, Michael W. McElwain, Rob Zellem, Jessica Noviello, Aki Roberge, Alden S. Jurling, Richard J. Cartwright
Items.Title: Capabilities for the Habitable Worlds Observatory’s high-resolution imager
Items.Abstract: The HWO Technology Maturation Project Office (HTMPO) recently released a call for US-led studies for instruments for transformative astrophysics, including a NUV/Optical/NIR high spatial resolution imager (HRI). HRI could have many potential modes, including astrometry, imaging, and low-resolution spectroscopy, while also fulfilling the guiding and some wavefront sensing modes for the entire observatory. The proposed HRI concepts are meant to be responsive to a wide range of astrophysics science cases detailed by the community. The call for instrument studies defines bounding conditions for mass, power, and volume, as well as information about the optical, thermal, and mechanical interfaces for EACs 4 and 5.  The HRI Coordination Group developed these bounding conditions while incorporating science and engineering feedback, which we include in this presentation. NASA supports collaborative efforts for instrument studies, both internal to the US and abroad.

Items.Authors: Anna Rahim
Items.Title: Cascade adaptive optics with a second stage based on a Zernike wavefront sensor for exoplanet observations: in-lab validation on the European Southern Observatory/GHOST testbed in broadband light
Items.Abstract: Direct imaging of exoplanets is limited by residual wavefront errors after extreme adaptive optics correction, reducing contrast and preventing the detection of faint companions.   We implemented a cascaded adaptive optics system with a secondary Zernike wavefront sensor loop to correct these residual errors. Tested on the ESO GHOST testbed, the loop reduces wavefront errors, improves stability, and increases coronagraphic contrast in monochromatic light.  In broadband light with spectral widths over 20%, removing non-common path aberrations improves contrast by a factor of ten. Preliminary tests have validated the use of an artificial intelligence-based controller, designed to stabilize the loop and extend the sensor’s dynamic range under challenging observing conditions.  This cascaded system demonstrates strong performance and offers a promising upgrade path for current high-contrast instruments and future extremely large telescope exoplanet imagers.

Items.Authors: Rémi Soummer, Iva Laginja, Emiel Por, Raphaël Pourcelot, Sarah Steiger, Bryony Nickson, Alexis Lau, Pierre Baudoz, Jules Fowler, Raphaël Galicher, Tyler Groff, Rebecca Jensen-Clem, Dimitri Mawet, Johan Mazoyer, Michael McElwain, Lane Meier, Axel Potier, Laurent Pueyo, Susan Redmond, Scott Will, Neil Zimmerman
Items.Title: CATKit2-HCI: a collaborative framework for advancing high-contrast coronagraph testbeds
Items.Abstract: High-contrast exoplanet imaging requires dedicated laboratory testbeds for coronagraph technology development. The CATKit2-High-Contrast-Imaging (CATKit2-HCI) international collaboration unites groups operating coronagraph testbeds using CATKit2, an open-source Python infrastructure controlling hardware via a fast, C++ Client-Server architecture.   Our goal is to develop and share a common architecture and tools across facilities, fostering collaboration and accelerating progress. A key objective is to avoid duplication of effort and facilitate more direct comparison of results obtained at different testbeds. We are developing a common framework for wavefront sensing and control, standardized file outputs, visualization, and performance metrics. Formalized by a Collaboration Agreement, this initiative also facilitates the exchange of students and postdoctoral researchers, and is open to expand to other high-contrast coronagraph testbeds.

Items.Authors: Scott C. Chapman, Eve Vavagiakis, Jordan Wheeler, Michael Niemack, Jason Austermann, Johannes Hubmayr, Anthony Huber, James Burgoyne
Items.Title: CCAT: development of an MKIDs array for a 410GHz imager/polarimeter module
Items.Abstract: Prime-Cam, one of the first-light instruments for the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope developed by the  CCAT Collaboration, will accommodate seven modules, including an off-central 410 GHz camera. The 410GHz  instrument is a fully funded second generation module for CCAT, to be developed as a collaboration between  UBC/NRC-HAA and Duke University. With atmospheric loading in the 410GHz window being significantly  higher than at 350GHz (but substantially better than 850GHz), we assess the design of an array of ∼7,000 TiN  MKIDs optimized for use at 410GHz, for a total of 21,000 MKIDs over 3 arrays. We explore mapping speed  versus detector number, and optimal Qi/Qc and responsivity for the 410GHz window atop Cerro Chajnantor.  The detectors will be designed in frequency to be efficiently readout with the Gen-2 RFSoC-based two octave  readout, with over 4000 detectors per RFSoC.

Items.Authors: Paul Hickson, Micah Piva, Shaojie Chen, Suresh Sivanandam
Items.Title: Characterization of Kr and Xe pencil-type spectral lamps for the GIRMOS Calibration System
Items.Abstract: The Gemini Infrared Multi-Object Spectrograph (GIRMOS) is an integral-field spectrometer for the Gemini North observatory. Working with the Gemini North Adaptive Optics system, it will have a multi-object adaptive optics capability to provide increased resolution and sensitivity. The GIRMOS Calibration System (CAL) integrated within the GIRMOS instrument, provides photometric, spectroscopic and metrology calibration. For spectroscopic calibration, CAL will employ long-life (5,000 hr) Kr and Xe pencil-type gas discharge lamps. In order to characterize the emission from these lamps, we have performed laboratory measurements covering the wavelength range 900 - 2500 nm. Here we report absolute fluxes for the 135 most-prominent spectral lines in this region, spanning three orders of magnitude in intensity. The results confirm the suitability of these lamps for GIRMOS.

Items.Authors: Christian Fruck, Felipe Pedreros Bustos, Petr Janout, David Alaluf, Ronald Holzlöhner, Pierre Haguenauer, David Jenkins, Julienne Böttger, Mauro Centrone, Marco Faccini
Items.Title: Characterization of Rayleigh backscattering in CaNaPy: a sodium-LGS pulsed monostatic system
Items.Abstract: CaNaPy is an experimental Laser Guide Star (LGS) Adaptive Optics facility at the 1m ESA OGS telescope at the Observatorio del Teide, developed at ESO in collaboration with ESA, Durham University, IAC, INAF, and Microgate, with scientific collaborators from ANU and the RICAM institute. It aims for demonstrating pre-compensation of a sodium LGS uplink beam using a Pyramid wavefront sensor in a monostatic system.  In a monostatic system, one of the main challenges is to prevent laser stray light from the uplink path and Rayleigh scattering from reaching the wavefront sensor. This goal requires precisely synchronized mechanical chopper wheels in the up- and downlink optical paths. To gain detailed knowledge of the temporal properties of the return signal and to further fine tune the design and timing of the chopper wheels, the received pulses are sampled with a photomultiplier tube. We highlight technical aspects of the implementation and report on first measurements using this approach.

Items.Authors: Vianak Naranjo, Thomas Bertram, Yared Reinarz, Arne Bramigk, Harry Marth, Wim Pessemier
Items.Title: Characterization of the cryogenic METIS SCAO modulator
Items.Abstract: The METIS SCAO modulator is a motorized cryogenic tip-tilt mirror in charge of high precision circular motion that has to be synchronized with the integration time of the wavefront sensor detector, reaching up to 1000 circles per second. We present the results of the complete characterization of the modulator under cryogenic conditions, showing that the device complies with the specification of the SCAO module at the required operating temperature of 70K.

Items.Authors: Andrea Occhiuzzi, Elia Battistelli, Paolo de Bernardis, Fabio Columbro, Luca Lamagna, Silvia Masi, Edvige Celasco, Flavio Gatti
Items.Title: Characterization of the multi-mode TES detectors for the LSPE-SWIPE instrument
Items.Abstract: The detection of inflationary B-modes in CMB polarization is highly challenging and requires very sensitive instruments, achievable through large detector arrays or a multi-mode approach. We characterise multi-mode Ti/Au TES detectors for LSPE-SWIPE, with Tc~550mK, photon-noise-limited performance, and ~30ms time constants. Each detector is coupled to a multi-mode feedhorn via a mode-filtering waveguide that propagates the first few tens of modes. TESs were characterised at 300 mK under different background loads. Thermal conductance, saturation power, and noise-equivalent power were derived from voltage–current curves, while responsivity, optical efficiency, and time constant were measured using a coherent calibration source under flight-representative conditions. Combined with pixel beam measurements, the results agree with expectations from electromagnetic simulations.

Items.Authors: Huatao Zhang, Youwei Xie, Dejing Ni, Liang Wang, Fujia Du, Jiajia Wu, Kai Zhang, Jean Louis Lizon
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: design of software architecture
Items.Abstract: The Canary Hybrid Optical high-Resolution Ultra-stable Spectrograph (CHORUS) is a next-generation visible and ultraviolet spectrograph designed for the Gran Telescopio Canarias. This paper provides an overview of the control software architecture of CHORUS, which is designed as an integral part of the GTC Control System. The main components described are the Mechanisms Control System, responsible for controlling all moving mechanisms; the Data Acquisition System, which interfaces with the detectors; the Data Factory (DF) system, tasked with data reduction, storage, and quality control; the Instrument Library, which coordinates all instrument devices for scientific observations; and the Sequencer Library, which manages the execution of complex operational and scientific sequences in close coordination with the telescope. This modular architecture will ensure a robust, scalable, and maintainable system for the lifetime of the instrument.

Items.Authors: Jing Chen, Mingyi Ding, Liang Wang, Huatao Zhang, Jean Louis Lizon, Kai Zhang
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: design of the exposure time calculator
Items.Abstract: The Canary Hybrid Optical high-Resolution Ultra-stable Spectrograph (CHORUS) is an echelle spectrograph developed for 10.4m GTC in Spain. The instrument features a dual-band design, providing spectral resolutions of >25,000 in the UV band and >120,000 in the visible band. To support the observation planning and optimize the scheduling, we developed an exposure time calculator (ETC) to evaluate the data quality of CHORUS for different targets under various conditions. The ETC enables efficient estimation of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and photon-noise limited radial velocity (RV) precision by incorporating realistic models of stellar spectrum, sky background, atmospheric transmission, telescope and instrument throughput, detector characteristics, and observing conditions such as seeing and airmass. The ETC developed for CHORUS provides SNR prediction and exposure time determination. In this paper, we present the software architecture, working flows, and functionalities of CHORUS-ETC.

Items.Authors: Liang Wang, Jing Chen, Mingyi Ding, Kai Zhang, Jean-Louis Lizon, Shengrun Liu
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: end-to-end simulation of two-dimensional echelle spectrum
Items.Abstract: The Canary Hybrid Optical high-Resolution Ultra-stable Spectrograph (CHORUS) is an echelle spectrograph to be installed on the Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC) in Spain. We developed an end-to-end simulation framework to generate two-dimensional spectral data for CHORUS. This framework uses ZEMAX spot diagrams as input and accounts for various stellar parameters. It models different observing conditions, including atmospheric transparency, seeing, airmass, and the total throughput of the instrument. The PSF at different positions on the CCD is modeled by convolving the fiber illumination profile with the optical PSF derived from ZEMAX. Various noises are incorporated, including photon noise, sky background, CCD readout noise, and dark current. The simulated two-dimensional spectra are used to test the CHORUS data reduction pipeline and to refine instrument parameters. Using this framework, we concluded that the key characteristics of CHORUS can fulfill the scientific requirements.

Items.Authors: Huiqi Ye, Jean-Louis Lizon, Zhen Tang, Kai Zhang
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: fiber link and fiber scrambling
Items.Abstract: We present the design of fiber link system and test results of a double-scrambler prototype and a dynamic scrambler prototype for CHORUS on GTC. The double scrambling system incorporates two octagonal fibers, and a relay optics which is composed of two identical doublets. The first lens images the end-face of input fiber at the focus of the second lens. The second lens projects the pupil on the end of outgoing fiber. The scrambler shows near field scrambling gain 29000 and wonderful far field scrambling. The measured optical throughput efficiency is 85.7% and FRD efficiency at F/3.16 is 92.5%. The dynamic scrambling system includes one octagonal fiber, and two voice coil activators which are used to agitate the fiber vertically and horizontally. The SNR of coherent laser with dynamic scrambler is improved from ~4.7 to ~55.6, which has been very close to that of non-coherent lamp 62.1.

Items.Authors: Liang Tang, Jean-Louis Lizon, Qiqige Xin, Bin Yu, Xiaolin Huang, Jiajia Wu, Huiqi Ye, Kai Zhang
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: final design of the calibration system
Items.Abstract: CHORUS is a high-resolution spectroscopic instrument under development for the 10.4 m Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC) at La Palma, Spain. One of its main scientific drivers is the detection and characterization of extra-solar planets. The visible band spectrograph (VIS) of the instrument offers spectral resolution of R>120000 at the visible band and is vacuum stabilized for performing high precision radial velocity measurements. The UV band spectrograph (UVS) of the instrument has a resolving power of R>25000 and allows for stellar activity monitoring. Aiming at a radial velocity precision at the sub-m/s level, CHORUS has a dedicated calibration system enabling high precision calibration under different observation modes. We describe here the final design and prototyping of the CHORUS calibration system (CLS).

Items.Authors: Kai Zhang, Shengrun Liu, Yuan Liang, Liang Wang, Qiqige Xin, Jean-Louis Lizon, Jianrong Shi
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: optical design of the UV band spectroscopic chain
Items.Abstract: The Canary Hybrid Optical high-Resolution Ultra-stable Spectrograph (CHORUS) is a high-precision spectrograph facility designed for the 10.4 m Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC). It employs a dual-band configuration, combining an ultraviolet-band spectrograph (UVS) with a visible-band spectrograph (VIS), to optimize performance for faint-object detection in the UV and for extreme precision radial velocity (EPRV) measurements in the visible band. This paper presents a complete UV spectroscopic chain from the Nasmyth focus to the science detector, in which the UVS is fed by fore-optics rather than by a fiber link. This design delivers a spectral resolution of R ≥ 25,000 over the wavelength range 310–420 nm, providing strong competitiveness for spectroscopic observations in the ultraviolet. The resulting capability will support studies of stellar activity relevant to EPRV science and will also enable frontier research in areas such as galactic archaeology and related fields.

Items.Authors: Kai Zhang, Bernard Delabre, Liang Wang, Shengrun Liu, Yuan Liang, Qiqige Xin, Jean-Louis Lizon, Xuesong Wang
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: optical design of the visible band spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The Canary Hybrid Optical high-Resolution Ultra-stable Spectrograph (CHORUS) is a high-precision spectrographic facility designed for the 10.4 m Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC). It employs a dual-band configuration, combining an ultraviolet-band spectrograph (UVS) with a visible-band spectrograph (VIS), to optimize performance for faint-object detection in the ultraviolet and for extreme precision radial velocity (EPRV) measurements in the visible. With its high-performance capabilities in EPRV, the VIS will advance key scientific areas such as the search for habitable exoplanets and the study of planetary atmospheres. This paper presents the optical design of the VIS, which integrates a pupil slicer with an anamorphic white-pupil system to achieve a very high spectral resolution of R ≥ 120,000 across the wavelength range of 420–780 nm. The spectrograph employs two spectral arms (G and R) to accommodate all the spectra from two parallel science fibers.

Items.Authors: Fujia Du, Shuai Chen, Hao Chen, Huatao Zhang, Dejing Ni, Jiajia Wu, Kai Zhang, Jean-Louis Lizon
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: the final design of Instrument Control Electronics
Items.Abstract: CHORUS (Canary Hybrid Optical high-Resolution Ultra-stable Spectrograph) is a high-resolution, ultra-stable spectrograph to be installed on the Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC). Its key feature is achieving an instrumental radial-velocity precision of 10 cm/s - an extremely demanding performance target that drives the design of its subsystems. The CHORUS Instrument Control Electronics (ICE) is responsible for governing all instrument subsystems, including over 20 motorized stages, more than 60 sensors, and several calibration lamps. To meet CHORUS stringent requirements, this paper summarizes the core characteristics of the CHORUS ICE, presents the test performance of key prototypes (e.g., the image stabilization system, motion control system, and dynamic scrambler system), and provides an overview of the ICE final design—with a focus on the spectrograph’s most critical and innovative aspects.

Items.Authors: Dejing Ni, Huatao Zhang, Fujia Du, Huiqi Ye, Liang Tang, Kai Zhang, Jean Louis Lizon
Items.Title: CHORUS on GTC: the image stabilization system
Items.Abstract: CHORUS (Canary Hybrid Optical High-Resolution Ultra-Stable Spectrograph) is expected to become a powerful scientific instrument for precise radial velocity measurements. This paper introduces an image stabilization system designed for the instrument Front-End Unit (FEU). The FEU optics projects the input beam onto a tip-tilt mirror. The Image Stabilization system utilizes image processing methods to calculate real-time centroid shifts caused by atmospheric turbulence and telescope tracking errors, then applies tip-tilt correction to maintain highly stable focusing of the scientific target's spot at the fiber-injection interface. An experimental system, comprising a seeing simulation system and an image stabilization system, was developed to validate the approach. Experimental results demonstrate that the method's performance meets scientific requirements.

Items.Authors: Ruoyu Zhou, Renbin Yan, Yutong Qiao
Items.Title: CMOS-optimized echelle design for AMASE high-resolution IFU spectroscopy: achieving near-peak blaze efficiency for key emission lines
Items.Abstract: We present a system-level optical design for a high-resolution (R~19000) Integral Field Unit (IFU) spectrograph for the AMASE project. The front-end utilizes 20cm f/10 Ritchey-Chretien telescopes with telecentric correctors to feed a Hexagonal Close-Packed microlens array, sampled by 1980 octagonal fibers for excellent near-field scrambling. To overcome efficiency drops at critical wavelengths, we employ a modular architecture with a 97.11 g/mm, 56-deg blaze Echelle grating. This aligns key emission lines (e.g., H-alpha, H-beta, [O-III]) near the blaze peak to maximize actual throughput. Crucially, this subdues anamorphic magnification and relaxes the camera speed to a manufacturable f/2.16, unlocking the integration of 150-Megapixel large-format CMOS sensors (Sony IMX411). To match the 54mm detector limits, the system is segmented into five identical spectrographs, delivering a scalable platform for multiplexed IFU surveys.

Items.Authors: Arianna Saba, Giorgio Savini, Philip Windred, Richard Archer, Giovanna Tinetti, Ian Stotesbury, Marcell Tessenyi, Fabio Favata
Items.Title: Commissioning Mauve, a spectrophotometric UV satellite
Items.Abstract: Mauve is a 16U small satellite designed and operated by Blue Skies Space Ltd, built on a C3S platform with a fine guidance system provided by ISISPACE. The payload incorporates commercial off-the-shelf components, including a 13 cm MediaLario telescope (adapted from laser-communication use), a commercially modified fibre from CeramOptec, and a standard configuration NEXOS spectrometer from Avantes. Mauve was launched on 28 November 2025 into a 10:30 LTDN Sun-synchronous low-earth orbit. The mission is designed to perform spectrophotometric measurements of bright stars across the 200–700 nm range to support stellar and exoplanet science. In this paper, we present the Mauve design architecture, commissioning results, and the initial performance of the spacecraft. At the time of submission (six days after launch), the mission remains in the early operations phase. Updates to this abstract may follow as commissioning progresses in the coming weeks and months.

Items.Authors: Rima Islam, Abani Shankar Nayak, Aline Dinkelaker, Kalaga V. Madhav, Martin M. Roth
Items.Title: Commissioning the AIP's ultrafast laser Inscription facility: defining the parameter space for type-I waveguide fabrication
Items.Abstract: This work details the iterative statistical optimization of the femtosecond-based ultrafast laser inscription system—specifically pulse energy, repetition rate, translation speed, and scan density to achieve Type-1 positive refractive-index modifications. We present the resulting fabrication recipe for single-mode, high-throughput waveguides optimized for the astronomical J-band (1300-1400 nm). By achieving precise Mode Field Diameter (MFD) matching with standard optical fibers, we ensure low insertion loss. The optimization of parameter space is critical for the fabrication of complex devices, such as photonic reformatters, beam combiners, and pupil remappers, for future deployment at the CHARA array and Calar Alto Observatory.

Items.Authors: Maduranthahan Viveganandam
Items.Title: Compact high-resolution spectrograph for Alt-Azimuth mounted Cassegrain telescopes: optical design and simulation
Items.Abstract: Alt-azimuth mounted telescopes with Cassegrain focus offer affordability and versatility but often lack the clearance needed to attach standard commercial spectrographs. To overcome this limitation, we developed a compact, cost-effective, high-resolution spectrograph specifically designed for seamless integration with such telescopes. The instrument incorporates a 1200 grooves/mm diffraction grating and a narrow slit aperture, with optical performance evaluated using Zemax OpticStudio ray-tracing simulations. Results confirm effective spectral dispersion, accurate focusing of RGB wavelengths, and strong agreement with theoretical expectations. Aberration analysis shows negligible higher-order effects, with only slight spherical aberration present. Overall, the spectrograph demonstrates excellent image quality and validates a practical, accessible solution for high-resolution astronomical spectroscopy.

Items.Authors: Jinyuan Yuan, Ting Zhou, Yangfan Jiang, Bin Liu, Yuxi Ruan, Yanguang Yu, Haiping Du
Items.Title: Compressive sensing-based distance and speed measurement with FMCW self-mixing interferometry
Items.Abstract: This study introduces compressed sensing (CS) to Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) self-mixing interferometry (SMI) for distance and speed measurements. The CS algorithm effectively reconstructs signals at sub-Nyquist sampling rates, reducing hardware costs and enhancing real-time performance. Using a Subspace Pursuit (SP) algorithm, the proposed method achieves high accuracy with reduced computational complexity. Simulations validate that measurement errors remain within 10⁻³ under low sampling rates. While developed for compact laser sensing systems, the underlying CS-based sparse reconstruction framework offers direct applicability to optical interferometric data processing in astronomy. This technique offers a cost-effective, high-precision solution for industrial and scientific applications requiring real-time measurements.

Items.Authors: Reuben Neate, Tinus Stander
Items.Title: Concept design of a single-IC integrated 183 GHz direct detection water vapour radiometer
Items.Abstract: The requirements for an 183 GHz water vapour radiometer (WVR) are considered, and design specifications are proposed. The proposed design is found to be achievable through single-IC integration of a radiometer using a 165 GHz direct detection receiver, consisting of a calibration switch with controllable thermal load, low noise amplifier (LNA), and power detector. The design is found to produce a compact, lightweight WVR, suitable for integration in confined spaces. The single-IC integration also lends itself to arrayed receiver design, of which a concept is presented.

Items.Authors: Johan Kosmalski, Luca Pasquini
Items.Title: Concepts for a large field corrector and Atmospheric Dispersion Compensator for the Nasmyth focus of the Very Large Telescope
Items.Abstract: The Nasmyth foci of the four VLT 8m telescopes at paranal Observatory offer the largest Field of View available for Multi-Object-Spectrographs (MOS). Given the several interface restrictions present, so far none of these foci has been equipped with an Atmospheric Dispersion Compensator (ADC), that, on the other hand, could be highly beneficial for MOS observations over a large wavelength range. In this work we present two new optical concepts that provide a full Nasmyth corrected field, that respect the VLT interface prescription.

Items.Authors: Rafael Alves de Souza Ribeiro, René Laporte, Antonio Nazareno Uchoa de Oliveira Filho, Alex Cavaliéri Carciofi, Ariane Cristina Fonseca Silva, Claudia Lúcia Mendes de Oliveira, Tommy Lazaneo Zirnberger
Items.Title: Conceptual design of a dual-arm imager with polarimetric capability for the T80-S telescope
Items.Abstract: We present the conceptual development of a new dual-arm imaging instrument for the T80-South telescope, designed to extend the capabilities by combining broadband and narrowband imaging with linear polarimetry.     The system splits the incoming beam into two optical channels optimized for complementary spectral coverage, enabling simultaneous acquisition of broad- and narrowband images.     A polarization modulator and a dual-beam analyzer provide differential measurements of orthogonal linear polarization states. Several analyzer configurations and architectures are currently being evaluated to balance instrumentation requirements. The polarimetric subsystem is being optimized for mid-precision levels for bright sources while maintaining a larger field of view than conventional narrow-field polarimeters.    Scientific goals include wide-area mapping of interstellar polarization, characterization of circumstellar scattering, and narrowband polarimetric studies of emission-line structures.

Items.Authors: Naoshi Murakami, Shunya Sato, Kenta Yoneta, Jun Nishikawa, Keigo Enya, Hajime Kawahara, Takayuki Kotani, Shota Miyazaki, Aoi Takahashi, Toru Yamada
Items.Title: Conceptual study of auxiliary optical module for multi-band high-contrast wavefront control
Items.Abstract: An auxiliary optical module aimed at enhancing multi-band capability of wavefront control has been proposed and developed as part of the technological efforts at the coronagraph testbed EXIST (Murakami et al., Proc. SPIE, 2020 and 2024). We expect this technology to enable efficient spectral characterization of exoplanets across a broad wavelength range, as well as planetary surface mapping via multi-band photometric variations. We performed numerical simulations to validate the concept of this optical module. Although the simulations are simplified and preliminary, the results suggest that very high contrast can be achieved simultaneously and independently across multiple spectral bands separated by more than 20% in bandwidth.

Items.Authors: Paweł Rukat
Items.Title: Construction of a laboratory model of an adaptive optics module for an amateur telescope
Items.Abstract: This work evaluates adaptive optics for small amateur telescopes using simulations of Kolmogorov turbulence, Shack–Hartmann sensing and segmented-mirror correction. Early results for a 0.3 m system under r₀ = 0.05 m turbulence showed phase amplitudes of 2–2.5 λ and rms reduction from about λ/1.3 to λ/4.2 using three-degree-of-freedom segments. The current study extends this framework toward a hybrid architecture by introducing liquid-crystal phase modulators for high-order correction. The combined system, in which the segmented mirror removes low-order terms and the LC device refines residuals, is expected to provide near-diffraction-limited performance and guide the design of a compact laboratory AO demonstrator.

Items.Authors: Davide Deiana, Guido Vecchia
Items.Title: Construction of the dome and telescope structure of the ELT
Items.Abstract: The telescope Main Structure and the Dome of the ELT are being procured by ESO as an integrated system together with the auxiliary building and the service plants and are supplied by the ACe Consortium. The contract was signed in May 2016 and the path to final delivery has proven to be challenged by intricate, multi-faceted technical roadblocks emerging from every discipline.  The progress is visible and tangible; the primary and secondary structures are complete, and we are nearing completion of the physical installations (e.g. electrical, and fluid distribution), with commissioning just around the corner. However, there are various challenges yet to be overcome. In this paper we will describe the progress and achievements of the site construction so far as well as give an outline of the challenges involved in maintaining quality, productivity, and spirits high when building a giant telescope in the middle of the desert at 3000m.

Items.Authors: Awatif Hiti, Gabriel Tayama, Simon Thibault
Items.Title: Contactless magnetorheological PDMS membrane for high-stroke deformable mirrors
Items.Abstract: We present a contactless deformable mirror based on a PDMS membrane embedded with magnetite nanoparticles and actuated by a 37-magnet array. The 50 mm-diameter, 275 µm-thick membrane achieved deformations up to 0.97 mm under magnetic fields of 21–77 mT, with surface roughness between 3 and 7 nm. Experimental measurements and COMSOL simulations showed excellent agreement, confirming the potential of magnetic actuation to overcome the spatial limitations of conventional mirrors. This approach enables high-stroke, optical-quality deformation for adaptive optics applications in astronomy, laser communications, and vision science.

Items.Authors: Thomas Birbacher, Julio Pino Jiménez, Jonah T. Hansen, Germain Garreau, Adrian M. Glauser, Sascha P. Quanz
Items.Title: Control and compensation mechanisms for cryogenic broadband nulling
Items.Abstract: Deep broadband cryogenic nulling is a prerequisite for the LIFE space mission to characterize habitable-zone exoplanets. While the top-level requirements on Optical Path Difference (OPD) and intensity mismatch are theoretically defined, achieving them across the 4 to 18.5 µm bandpass under cryogenic conditions remains an unresolved engineering challenge. Even sub-arcsecond errors in alignment or coating mismatches at the sub-percent level may be critical at the required nulls.    To prepare for the Nulling Interferometry Cryogenic Experiment (NICE), we present potential frameworks for the control and compensation of quasi-static chromatic, polarization, and alignment errors. Our reference strategy involves a careful static alignment and pre-compensation for cooling down, and to use targeted individual mechanisms. An alternative approach is the adaptive nuller. We compare the two and evaluate their suitability for a high-sensitivity, deep-contrast cryogenic nulling interferometer.

Items.Authors: Mingyeong Yang, Sang-Hyun Chun, Yongmin Yoon, Yunjong Kim, Yongseok Lee, Sungwook E. Hong, Minhee Hyun, Jae-Woo Kim, Ho Seong Hwang
Items.Title: Control software development for A/K-SPEC guiding, focusing, acquisition, and atmospheric dispersion correction systems
Items.Abstract: The All-Sky Spectroscopic Survey (A-SPEC) is an all-sky, large-volume, multi-object spectroscopic survey targeting galaxies with K_s < 13.75. The K-SPEC instrument system, developed for A-SPEC, is designed to deliver precise and efficient spectroscopic observations. This paper presents the design and implementation of the control software for the K-SPEC GFA (Guiding, Focusing, and Acquisition) and ADC (Atmospheric Dispersion Correction) systems. The software automates key observational procedures, providing both low-level device control and system monitoring. The K-SPEC GFA control system provides three core functions: simultaneous control of multiple guide cameras, acquisition of images from these cameras, and computation of guiding offsets from the acquired images. The K-SPEC ADC control system compensates for atmospheric dispersion by dynamically adjusting two prism motors in response to telescope pointing information.

Items.Authors: José Leonardo Garcés Medina, Enrique Colorado, Ximena Zepeda, Itzel Gonzalez-Ochoa, Jorge Fuentes-Fernández, Jaime Ruíz-Díaz-Soto, Fernando Ángeles, Alejandro Farah, Sebastián Sánchez
Items.Title: Control system design and implementation for EBANO, a low-cost scanning spectrograph at the OAN San Pedro Mártir
Items.Abstract: EBANO is a low-cost scanning spectrograph for the 84-cm telescope at San Pedro Mártir. Its control system integrates an EMCCD detector, a linear stage, and two custom COTS-based rotary stages that provide the fine angular motion required for wavelength scanning. EBANO is the first instrument designed under the observatory’s new client–server architecture, featuring a Python-based API for configuration, sequencing, monitoring, and network-based image transfer. The system includes an isolated local engineering interface and a robust software environment tolerant to unexpected power losses. This work summarizes the architecture, implementation, and current status of the EBANO control system, which will serve as a template for future OAN-SPM instruments.

Items.Authors: Hao A. Li, Jialin Pan, Qishuai Lu, Shouwei Hu
Items.Title: Cooperative control of a dual-stage compliant actuator for high-precision positioning
Items.Abstract: To address the trade-off between large stroke and nanometer resolution, this paper proposes a cooperative control strategy for a dual-stage compliant actuator. The system integrates a long-stroke coarse stage with a high-bandwidth compliant fine stage. Addressing inter-stage coupling and friction, a master-slave architecture featuring Zynq SoC dual-core parallel processing is designed. A robust controller compensates for fine-stage hysteresis, while the SoC allocates low-frequency signals to the coarse stage and high-frequency errors to the fine stage in real-time. Experimental results demonstrate the system achieves a 4 mm travel range, 5 nm positioning accuracy, and a 500 ms settling time. This provides an effective solution for segmented mirror active optics control.

Items.Authors: Michael J. Freyberg, Isabella Castel-branco
Items.Title: Correlating high-energy background detections between SRG/eROSITA and XMM-Newton in the magnetosphere environment
Items.Abstract: Space-based X-ray imaging is currently hindered by background noise, which   principally originates from solar wind, coronal mass ejections and Galactic   Cosmic Rays. Whilst noise is inevitable, understanding it allows for   optimised mitigation. Our project aims to characterise the high energy space   environment by correlating the background enhancements detected between   XMM-Newton and SRG/eROSITA, wherein we explicitly compare their respective   environments -- near-Earth and L2 -- by studying individual solar particle   clouds' propagation. Enhancements at L2 were detected by eROSITA and sorted   using a statistical algorithm: these will then be cross-correlated with   XMM-Newton's near-Earth detections, with delays ranging from a few seconds for   relativistic particles and an hour for soft-proton clouds.   Spatially characterising the differentiated high-energy background environment   is essential to appropriately plan for future X-ray missions, such as the   upcoming NewAthena probe.

Items.Authors: Anna K. Vaskuri, Jordan Wheeler, Jason Austermann, Harshit Agarwal, Shannon Duff, Michael Vissers, Johannes Hubmayr, Joel Ullom
Items.Title: Cryogenic polarization response measurement system for long wavelength polarimetric detectors
Items.Abstract: We have recently developed a cryogenic polarization response measurement system based on a cryogenic stepper motor mounted on the 4 K stage used to characterize sub-Kelvin millimeter-wave polarization-sensitive detectors. The motor rotates an electrically-modulated cryogenic thinfilm blackbody source, Winston cone mirror, and custom-microfabricated wire-grid polarizer. In this work, the system is used to characterize the polarization response of sub-Kelvin polarimetric detectors across various spectral bands from 150 GHz to 850 GHz. When rotating the polarized source for a full revolution, one should see a detector response with two full periods of a sine wave, where the minimum is defined as the cross-polarization. We will present the polarization response measurements, compare the measured cross-polarization results against the simulations, provide breakout of the cross-polarization contributions, and estimate the corresponding combined expanded measurement uncertainty.

Items.Authors: Bruno V. Castilho, Márcio V. Vital de Arruda, Orlando Verducci, Jesulino B. dos Santos, Leandro H. dos Santos, Josimar A. Rosa, Clemens D. Gneiding, Beatriz S. Barbuy, Matteo Z. Genoni, Roberto Cirami, Stefano Covino, Igor Coretti
Items.Title: CUBES, the Cassegrain U-Band Efficient Spectrograph: the Calibration Unit for the UV
Items.Abstract: The Cassegrain U-Band Efficient Spectrograph (CUBES) for the ESO VLT is optimized for high-efficiency spectroscopy in the near-UV (300–405 nm) at R > 20,000 (and R ~ 7,000 in a lower-resolution mode). Achieving accurate calibration in this spectral region poses specific challenges, including the scarcity of suitable continuum and line sources and stringent stability requirements for flat-fielding and wavelength calibration. We present the final design of the CUBES Calibration Unit, which passed its Final Design Review in July 2025 and is now in the MAIT phase. The system provides flat-field, wavelength calibration, and illumination characterization through a dedicated optical path feeding the instrument at the Cassegrain focus. We describe the calibration strategy, the optical and mechanical architecture, the control electronics, and performance predictions. Installation at the VLT is planned for 2030.

Items.Authors: Julian Stürmer, Christopher Ritz, Carmen Feiz, Edoardo Redaelli, Stephen Watson, Joel Harman, Matteo Genoni, Walter Seifert, Lawrence Bissell, Luca Oggioni, Giorgio M. Pariani, Hans Dekker, Chris Waring, Roberto Cirami, Stefano Covino, Stefano Cristiani, Andreas Quirrenbach
Items.Title: CUBES: mechanical design and analysis for high-resolution UV spectroscopy on the VLT
Items.Abstract: The Cassegrain U-Band Efficient Spectrograph (CUBES) is a next-generation, high-resolution UV spectrograph for the Very Large Telescope (VLT), covering 300-405nm with R > 20000. We present the mechanical design and opto-mechanical analysis, including challenges and constraints that impacted the system layout and material choices. Finite Element Analysis verifies compliance with ESO standards. To mitigate variable gravity loads, we developed an active flexure compensation system to maximize optical performance.

Items.Authors: Lawrence Bissell, Ariadna Calcines Rosario, Walter Seifert, Hans Dekker, Gerardo Avila, Luca Oggioni, Giorgio Pariani, Matteo Genoni, Roberto Cirami, Stefano Covino
Items.Title: CUBES: optical design and analysis of the VLT’s high-resolution UV spectrograph past final design review
Items.Abstract: CUBES (Cassegrain U-Band Efficient Spectrograph) will be the most efficient UV spectrograph on an 8-10m telescope, exploiting the ESO VLT’s higher telescope efficiency relative to the ESO ELT in ground-based UV wavelengths. The instrument provides wavelength coverage over a range of 300-405nm, with high instrumental efficiency (>37%) and a resolving power of >20,000 (HR) and >6,000 (LR). This paper presents the finalised optical design and analysis of the system after the final design review. The optical subsystems detailed include: a pair of UV-optimized atmospheric dispersion correctors designed to function out to a zenith angle of 65°; high throughput HR and LR image slicers used to reformat the field-of-view; and a dispersion-compensating three-lens spectrographic camera design.

Items.Authors: Xiaobo Li
Items.Title: Current calibration status of Insight-HXMT
Items.Abstract: As China’s first X-ray astronomy satellite, Insight-HXMT has been successfully operating in orbit for more than eight years. Designed for timing and spectral studies of black holes and neutron stars, the mission carries three main payloads: the High Energy X-ray Telescope (HE), the Medium Energy X-ray Telescope (ME), and the Low Energy X-ray Telescope (LE). Together, these instruments provide a unique combination of large effective area, broad energy band, and high timing resolution, enabling detailed investigations into high-energy astrophysical phenomena. In this paper, we present a comprehensive overview of the current in-orbit calibration status of Insight-HXMT. We report updates on key calibration parameters including energy gain, energy resolution, effective area, and timing performance. The calibration results support the high-quality data analysis for ongoing and future studies of compact objects and transient events.

Items.Authors: Timothy E. Pickering, Kyle B. Westfall, J. Xavier Prochaska, Joseph F. Hennawi, Debora Pelliccia, Ryan J. Cooke, Timothy Ellsworth-Bowers, Frederick B. Davies, Feige Wang, Dusty Reichwein, Brad Holden, Max Brodheim
Items.Title: Current status of and future plans for PypeIt, a Python-based spectroscopic data reduction pipeline
Items.Abstract: PypeIt (pronounced "pipe it") is a Python package that enables semi-automated processing and data reduction of optical/near-IR spectroscopic data. PypeIt is designed to be a general purpose data reduction pipeline and currently supports ~50 spectrographs on ~18 telescopes.The algorithms within PypeIt build on decades of development on previous data reduction pipelines to produce robust science-grade data products.    With the release of version 2.0.0, PypeIt enters a more mature stage of development with a codified governance structure, a better defined software versioning system, and a more consistent release schedule. Efforts are ongoing to work more closely with facilities that PypeIt supports to improve its reliability and performance when handling data from those facilities. These efforts have been aided by an award from the NSF's Pathways to Enable Open-Source Ecosystems (POSE) program.

Items.Authors: Derya Öztürk Çetni, Gizay Yolalan, Kemal Rüzgar, Burak Bülent Güçsav, Ebru Uzunçam, Cahit Yeşilyaprak, Deniz Becker
Items.Title: DAGOS: a multi-wavelength optical simulator integrated at the Nasmyth platform for AO and coronagraphic calibration at the DAG telescope
Items.Abstract: This study presents the design, laboratory validation, and full integration of the DAG Optical Simulator (DAGOS), a multi-wavelength and multi-field test platform developed for the 4 m DAG Telescope. DAGOS reproduces the F#14.2 beam, pupil geometry, and field coverage through a reflective optical layout, adjustable multi-fiber sources spanning 630–2000 nm, and kinematic mechanisms. Laboratory tests confirmed diffraction-limited performance at key planes, including the DM, SLM, Lyot, and science focal plane. The system provides stable and repeatable illumination for coronagraphic mask testing, adaptive optics calibration, and NCP aberration monitoring. Final integration on the Nasmyth platform verified reliable light injection and daytime AO calibrations, positioning DAGOS as a fully operational simulator supporting both laboratory development and on-telescope verification.

Items.Authors: Daniel Lancaster, Stefan Kraus, Jyotirmay Paul, Sorabh Chhabra, Owain Snaith
Items.Title: Delay line mirror design and metrology testing for the BIFROST instrument
Items.Abstract: BIFROST is a near-infrared (1-1.7um) beam combiner and spectrograph that will be installed at the Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) as part of the ASGARD array. To achieve fringes with an astronomical interferometer the beams of each telescope must be path length matched to bellow their coherence length. BIFROST will rely primarily on the large delay lines of the VLTI and other instruments (HEIMDELLR), but additional delay correction will be needed during operation. This small amount of delay correction needs to be smooth and accurate whilst being directly implemented into the BIFROST servers. This paper will discuss the delay actuator requirements needed to achieve science goals. Multiple actuators are tested and other design concepts are discussed. The final delay line actuator design is discussed and tested to show the performance meets all requirements. In addition the process of cophasing and metrological testing using the delay line mirror will be discussed.

Items.Authors: Tony J. Farrell, Nick Cerneaz, Lewis G. Waller, Ross Zhelem, Sana Syed, Satyam Mishra, Helen McGregor, Jahanzeb Zahoor, Mark Casali, Rolf Muller, Sambath Non, Slavko Mali, Urs Klauser, Vladimir Churilov, Yevgen Kripak, Zhemin Cai, Annino Vaccarella, Eckhart Spalding
Items.Title: Delivery and acceptance testing of the near infrared camera DIRAC instrument for the East Anatolia Observatory (DAG)
Items.Abstract: The DIRAC instrument (DAG InfraRed Adaptive optics Camera) has been built by Australian Astronomical Optics (AAO, Macquarie University, Australia) for the East Anatolia Observatory (Turkish - Doğu Anadolu Gözlemevi, DAG). DAG is a new 4-meter telescope with VIS/IR observation capability. It is located on the Konaklı-Karaya peak, near the city of Erzurum. One of the Nasmyth platforms provides will provide an AO optimized beam for instrumentation.    DIRAC provides the telescope with a 30" FoV near-infrared diffraction limited camera for use with the AO optimised beam. DIRAC will be used with a stellar coronagraph.    We examine the testing of the DIRAC instrument in Australia, reassembly at the telescope and acceptance testing of the instrument. As the AO system was not yet ready, we were unable to perform on-sky testing, but the testing in Australia confirmed the optical qualities of the instrument and on-sky commissioning will be completed in mid 2026.

Items.Authors: Christopher T. Ratliff, Renate Kupke, Phil Hinz, Matthew Radovan, Daren Dillon, Aaron Hunter, Brad Holden, Deno Stelter, Emily Plume, Javier Perez Soto, Nick MacDonald, Brian Peterson, Yuhui Wang, David Marques, Marc Kassis, Luke Gers
Items.Title: Design and development of a Hindle sphere optical test system for the calibration of the Keck 1 Telescope adaptive secondary mirror
Items.Abstract: The Keck 1 Telescope will be retrofitted with a new adaptive secondary mirror. To calibrate the surface figure of this large (~1.4m) deformable aspheric convex secondary mirror we will use a Hindle sphere optical test. Typically the Hindle sphere optic must be larger than the convex aspheric mirror (1.68m in this case). For our design we will utilize a system that consists of sub-apertures to reduce expense and difficulties in manufacturing a full size Hindle sphere. In this paper we describe the mechanical and optical design of the Hindle sub-aperture array system (referred to as Hindle array henceforth), how we rotate it, adjust the sub-aperture cells, and stitch together the wavefront data. We will show results from a small scale prototype that has been assembled and tested and then present the mechanical subsystem designs for the full scale Hindle array.

Items.Authors: Chun-Han Chou
Items.Title: Design and development of a multi-spectral imager payload for PM2.5–PM1 aerosol monitoring on the FORMOSAT-8 mission
Items.Abstract: In this paper, we present the multi-spectral imager design of a science-payload for air pollution monitoring, developed as part of the FORMOSAT-8D (FS-8D) program. These satellites will be placed in a sun-synchronous orbit. The first FORMOSAT-8 satellite already launched on 2025/11/29, and the science-payload will be installed on the fourth satellite (FS-8D). The payload is designed to monitor aerosol pollution in Taiwan, including PM1, PM2.5 and H2O. The science-payload consists of a VIS module and a SWIR module. The VIS module is designed to detect seven spectral bands for monitoring aerosol pollution. The SWIR module is designed to detect two spectral bands, enabling the identification of cirrus clouds and snow. Both modules have a swath greater than 200 km, enabling full aerosol data collection over Taiwan. The environmental validation of the optical payload is planned for completion in 2026, followed by the delivery of the flight model in 2027.

Items.Authors: Stephen P. Todd, Dan Dicken, Raziye Artan, Beth A. Biller, Cassandra Mercury, Katherine Morris, Vinooja Thurairethinam, Feng Zhao
Items.Title: Design and development of a near-IR integral field spectrograph for the HWO Coronagraph Instrument
Items.Abstract: The primary mission of the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) is to identify and characterise potentially habitable worlds. Spectra across a wide wavelength range are needed to cover multiple spectral features per molecule of interest. An integral field spectrometer (IFS), fed by a coronograph system, can be used to measure spectra from any planets within the nulled field of the coronograph, while also characterizing the residual speckles as a function of wavelength, enabling the contrast ratio to be further enhanced.  We show a proposed architecture for the IFS fed by the near-IR channel (0.8-1.7 micron) of the HWO Coronograph Instrument. The IFS must fully sample the speckle pattern at all wavelengths. Optical throughput must be maximised while also controlling cross-talk and stray light within the field. We outline the key design decisions and technology developments required to bring this system to the required technology readiness level.
